title: Limited Stopovers
statement: Flights between n cities are given as [from, to, price]. Return the cheapest price from city src to city dst using at most k stopovers (so at most k + 1 flights), or −1 if no such trip exists.

answerKey.pattern: Bellman–Ford limited to k + 1 rounds, relaxing from a copy of the previous round
keyPoints: Repeat k + 1 times: copy the costs, relax every flight from the old copy
The copy stops one round from using more than one new flight
edgeCases: A cheaper trip with more stops than allowed
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Dijkstra on (city, stops) states: also works, more code
Try every route of up to k + 1 flights: exponential

hints: Why can plain Dijkstra give the wrong answer?
The cheapest trip may use too many stopovers; the number of flights matters.
Run k + 1 rounds of relaxation, each from a snapshot of the previous round.
